subjects.name: Win Bigly: Persuasion in a World Where Facts Don't Matter

summary: A reading of Win Bigly, Dilbert cartoonist Scott Adams's 2017 book casting Donald Trump's 2016 campaign as the work of a near-mystical master persuader, and of the hypnosis and affirmation ideas behind it.

evidence.note: Host names the book being read and gives quick background on Adams and Dilbert
Adams's affirmations, Peter principle and self-help influences discussed at length
Book frames its story as June 2015 to November 2016 campaign period
Host contrasts persuasion myth with Trump as an authoritarian using an old far-right playbook
Adams's 98 percent prediction and Nate Silver branding stunt read and critiqued
First Republican debate insult and Trump's nickname tactics analysed

notes: Scott Adams lifespan end set to 2026 (died January 2026, after release). Primary theme could equally be electoral-politics; chose propaganda-media because the book's thesis is mass persuasion. fascism-far-right reflects the hosts' extended rebuttal comparing Trump to authoritarian playbooks and Hitler's rise. Brief nods to Dilbert's 1990s rise and The Religion War (2004) kept out of covered_span.
